worst_problem: The technique is loose: Mercury is called a 'light', 'benefic-friendly malefic' and exaltation as 'own resources' are invented terms, and the chart ruler's station ([S5]) trine the Ascendant is left out of the timing.
The January section gives the Neptune–Venus exact date as 2026-01-30 instead of 2027-01-30, which is a critical date error (type a).

The 90-day section turns trivial one-day Sun transits into confident infant-care forecasts ('fussy days', 'calm window for feeding and sleep', 'clingy stretch') that no tradition supports and that drift toward wellbeing predictions.

The fold handling understates what changes: it says only the angles and angle transits differ, mislabels Mars trine Moon as an angle transit, and leaves out [T8], [C3] and [S4a], which change between the two charts.

The 'where the two charts differ' section says the remaining differences are only a day or two, which is wrong for [T3]/[T25]. It also omits the angular planets that differ between the charts (Saturn on the Ascendant, Venus and Uranus on the IC in the later chart), so the uncertainty statement understates what the fold changes.

The fold section understates what differs: it tells parents everything else holds in both versions while omitting fold-dependent natal aspects and the Sun- and Mars-to-Ascendant and Midheaven transit dates, which reshape the November picture.
The sect teaching is botched by calling Mars 'helpful and constructive', and much of the interpretation is generic sign or keyword material, so the technique is thinner than the data supports.
The 90-day section leans on light Sun-transit filler ('easy day for fun', 'family treats') and leaves out the one shared slow-planet event, the Neptune station square natal Mars.

The 90-day section turns minor solar transits into day-by-day predictions about an infant's mood ('cozy day', 'fussier day', 'clinginess'), which is horoscope-style filler presented with false precision.

The difference section leaves out several timing divergences: T4 Saturn conjunction Venus dates differ (12-02/12-19 vs 11-29/12-22), Sun square MC is 2027-01-04 vs 2027-01-20, and T15 and S11a exist only in B. It also ignores Venus's detriment while calling Venus the most dependable gift.

The 90-day outlook is mostly a list of one-day Sun transits turned into parenting instructions, while the meaningful slow or station contacts that differ between charts ([T9], [T19], [S10a], [S1a]) get no ranges or weight.
Technique stays shallow: sect and dignity labels are quoted but not used to weigh factors, so minor solar transits get as much space as stations and the Uranus range.
The November and January summaries garble the body text: they imply [T3] falls on 2026-11-14, and they recast [T14] from a favourable day into a tired or sensitive one.

It omits chart B's Saturn square natal Sun (exact 2026-11-08 and 2027-01-12) while calling November gentle, so the timing picture is accurate only for chart A, and 'everything above is shared' contradicts its own chart-specific content.
The interpretation is thin on traditional technique beyond sect and dignity labels: no house rulerships, a faulty causal link for Saturn's dispositor, and a few filler lines stated as fact.

Synthesis is thin. Sections stand side by side without weighing the chart's real tensions: an exalted but out-of-sect Mars on the peregrine chart ruler, Saturn as both that ruler's dispositor and the Moon's square partner, and the MC falling in the 7th. Much of the advice slides into generic self-help.

The uncertainty section declares the angles 'firm' for a polar-latitude chart, where the Ascendant is extremely time-sensitive, and the natal section reads as separate factor-by-factor blocks rather than a weighed synthesis.

The 90-day section treats every fast Sun transit as roughly equal to the major slow events. It underweights the Neptune station conjunct the natal Sun and square natal Saturn/Uranus, and gives some solar transits keyword meanings that cut against the aspect, such as a square as a 'good day'.

The synthesis leaves out the chart's core tensions (the Sun in fall opposite the sect-light Moon, the Moon opposite Saturn, Venus as a sect benefic in detriment, Jupiter and Uranus in the 10th) and fills the Sun-transit calendar with stock phrases.

It invents a date range for the Sun's passage through the 7th house that the sheet's own later Capricorn transits contradict, and it reads hard aspects (Venus station square the Ascendant, Saturn square Mercury) as easy or favourable.

The uncertainty section ignores the high-latitude angle issue: the MC falls in house 8 and its meaning is never addressed, and the natal sections read as separate blocks without resolving tensions such as Saturn's condition.

The January section tells the parents the Sun square Midheaven hits 'the tenth house of public life', but the sheet puts the MC in whole sign house 9, so the reading misreads house placement at the very point where it gives timing advice.

The reading runs as a set of separate factor-by-factor sections, with thin weighing of contradictions (Jupiter dignified but in house 6, ruler in house 8, peregrine sect light) and a shallow uncertainty section that ignores the high-latitude effect on the angles.

The synthesis is thin. It misses the Moon–Jupiter mutual reception that joins the sect light to the chart ruler, and the 90-day section is a dated list of Sun transits with stock one-line glosses.
